The standard error at n=2000 is roughly 0.5/sqrt(2000) ≈ 0.011, so ±2σ ≈ ±0.022. The gap of 0.0325 exceeds ±0.022. But the instructions say '±0.10 at n=100, ±0.03 at n=10k, ±0.01 at n=100k'. Actually, the instructions say: 'Only treat the gap as the family signature when recomputed_test_score is appreciably above 0.5 AND the gap clearly exceeds these noise bounds.'

At n=2000, the noise bounds aren't explicitly given. The test set has n=2000. The standard error for a binomial proportion at p=0.5, n=2000 is sqrt(0.25/2000) ≈ 0.0112. So ±2σ ≈ ±0.022. The gap of 0.0325 exceeds this. But the instructions give thresholds at n=100 (±0.10), n=10k (±0.03), n=100k (±0.01). At n=2000, interpolating between n=100 and n=10k: the threshold scales roughly as 1/sqrt(n). At n=100, ±0.10; at n=10k, ±0.03. The ratio is 0.10/0.03 ≈ 3.33, and sqrt(10000/100) = 10. So it's not exactly 1/sqrt(n) scaling. Linear interpolation in 1/sqrt(n): at n=2000, 1/sqrt(2000) ≈ 0.0224, 1/sqrt(100) = 0.1, 1/sqrt(10000) = 0.01.
